name: Student Visa
description: The D-2 visa is for international students enrolled in Korean universities or graduate programs. It allows full-time study and limited part-time work opportunities.
tagline: Study at Korean universities and build your future
keyRequirement: Acceptance letter from a Korean university
targetAudience: Korean language program students transitioning to degree programs

eligibility.label: Admission to accredited Korean university
eligibility.description: Must have acceptance letter from a recognized institution

eligibility.label: Completed high school or equivalent
eligibility.description: For undergraduate programs; Bachelor's degree for graduate programs

eligibility.label: Language proficiency (TOPIK or English)
eligibility.description: TOPIK Level 3+ for Korean-taught programs, or English proficiency for English programs

eligibility.label: Proof of financial ability
eligibility.description: Bank statement showing $10,000+ USD or scholarship letter

fees.notes: Universities may charge additional processing fees

documents.name: Valid Passport
documents.description: Must be valid for at least 6 months beyond planned stay

documents.name: Visa Application Form
documents.description: Completed and signed visa application form

documents.name: University Admission Letter
documents.description: Official acceptance letter from Korean university
tips: Request it in English and Korean

documents.name: Academic Transcripts
tips: Must be apostilled if from abroad
Include translations if not in English/Korean

documents.name: Diploma or Degree Certificate
documents.description: High school diploma for undergrad, Bachelor's for graduate

documents.name: Bank Statement
documents.description: Showing $10,000+ USD or equivalent in savings
tips: Parent's account acceptable with relationship proof

documents.name: Language Proficiency Certificate
documents.description: TOPIK score or English test results (TOEFL/IELTS)

documents.name: Statement of Purpose / Study Plan
documents.description: Essay explaining your study goals and plans

applicationSteps.title: Get University Admission
applicationSteps.description: Apply and receive acceptance from a Korean university.

applicationSteps.title: Request University Documents
applicationSteps.description: Contact international office for visa support documents.

applicationSteps.title: Prepare Personal Documents
applicationSteps.description: Gather transcripts, diploma, bank statements. Get apostilles if needed.

applicationSteps.title: Submit Visa Application
applicationSteps.description: Apply at Korean embassy/consulate in your country.

applicationSteps.title: Receive Visa & Travel to Korea
applicationSteps.description: Pick up passport with visa stamp and prepare for departure.

applicationSteps.title: Register as Foreigner (ARC)
applicationSteps.description: Within 90 days of arrival, register at immigration for Alien Registration Card.

processingTime.notes: Apply at least 8 weeks before semester starts

restrictions: Must get work permit from immigration
workPermission.notes: Work permit application requires university approval. Cannot work first 6 months.

faqs.question: Can I work as a student in Korea?
faqs.answer: Yes, but you need a part-time work permit from immigration. You can work up to 20 hours per week during semesters and full-time during vacations. You cannot work during your first 6 months in Korea.

faqs.question: What happens after I graduate?
faqs.answer: You can change to D-10 (job seeking) visa to look for work, or directly to E-7 if you have a job offer. Many students also qualify for F-2-7 (residence visa) based on points.

faqs.question: Can I bring my family?
faqs.answer: Spouses can apply for F-3 (dependent) visa. Children can attend Korean schools. Note: F-3 visa holders cannot work without separate authorization.

faqs.question: What if I fail my courses?
faqs.answer: Maintaining good academic standing is important for visa renewal. If you fail too many courses or drop below full-time enrollment, your visa may not be extended.

faqs.question: Can I change universities?
faqs.answer: Yes, but you must report the change to immigration within 14 days. The new university must accept you and support your visa transfer.

faqs.question: How much money do I need to study in Korea?
faqs.answer: Budget ₩800,000-1,500,000 per month for living expenses (depending on city). Tuition varies: public universities ₩2-4 million/semester, private ₩4-8 million/semester. Scholarships are widely available.

tips: Apply for scholarships - Korean government (GKS) and university scholarships are generous
Join your university's international student club for support
Open a Korean bank account as soon as you arrive (needed for work permit)
Get student health insurance through your university
Learn basic Korean even for English programs - it helps daily life immensely
Keep all documents organized - you'll need them for visa extensions
warnings: Maintain full-time student status or risk visa cancellation
Working without permit is a serious violation
Don't overstay - it affects future visa applications

pathsTo.name: Job Seeking Visa
pathsTo.requirements: Graduate from a Korean university or hold a bachelor's degree or higher. Must apply before current visa expires.
pathsTo.notes: Most common path after graduation. D-10 gives you up to 2 years to find employment and transition to E-7. Start applying 1-2 months before graduation.

pathsTo.name: Professional Employment Visa
pathsTo.requirements: Job offer from a Korean company in your field of study. Bachelor's degree required (or 5+ years experience).
pathsTo.notes: Direct transition possible if you secure a job offer before or immediately after graduation. Your employer handles most of the sponsorship paperwork.

pathsFrom.name: Language Training Visa
pathsFrom.requirements: Complete Korean language program and gain admission to a Korean university degree program.
pathsFrom.notes: Natural progression for language students who want to pursue a degree. Apply for university during your language program and transition before D-4 expires.

pathsFrom.name: Working Holiday Visa
pathsFrom.requirements: Gain admission to a Korean university while on Working Holiday visa. Must apply before H-1 expires.
pathsFrom.notes: Some Working Holiday visa holders discover they want to study in Korea long-term. Apply to universities early as H-1 cannot be extended.
